prompt: Turn an empty Optional into a meaningful failure: use orElseThrow with the provided MissingSettingException so a missing or malformed setting reports which key was at fault.
explanation: Optional.ofNullable turns a possibly-null map value into an Optional, and map/filter then clean it up so every kind of "not usable" collapses into the same empty Optional. orElseThrow takes a Supplier, so the exception object is only constructed on the failing path -- and because it carries the key, the caller learns which setting was wrong instead of getting a bare NoSuchElementException. requireInt shows the pattern's real value: filtering bad text out first means one orElseThrow covers both missing and malformed values.
hints: find(key) is Optional.ofNullable(values.get(key)).map(String::trim).filter(v -> !v.isEmpty()) once the null key is handled.
require is one line: find(key).orElseThrow(() -> new MissingSettingException(key)).
For requireInt, filter with a regular expression such as "-?\\d+" before map(Integer::parseInt), so parsing can never fail.
